correctness.rationale: For the displayed edge-2sqrt(2) tetrahedron, the Cauchy face formula reduces projected area to max(4a,2(a+b+c)) for ordered absolute normal coordinates, and hull size is 3 iff a<b+c. Both cases of a>=1/sqrt(2) and a<1/sqrt(2) prove the minimum 2sqrt(2) and exactly twelve minimizers. Around each, an exact spherical chart gives s*sqrt(1-r^2)+b(phi)r with b>=2sqrt(2/3); uniform Taylor inversion and Jacobian integration produce two sector integrals. Elementary tan/cot integration proves b^-2 integrals equal 1/sqrt(2) and b^-4 integrals 7sqrt(2)/48 vs 5sqrt(2)/48. Normalizing by 12/(4pi) gives both claimed cubic coefficients and quotient slope sqrt(2)/24. Independently implemented convex hull and deterministic quadrature tests passed from the packaged checker. The computations alone are not treated as proof.

value.rationale: At the absolute minimum brightness the regular tetrahedron changes silhouette type. A geometric selection problem asks whether one type dominates an extremely area-efficient view. Despite global triangular-shadow frequency about 0.351, the near-minimum probability is 1/2 at leading order and has a sharp positive slope sqrt(2)/24 for triangular shadows. The effect is a natural joint geometric boundary law, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff or a trivial repeat of total frequencies, and the exact coefficients explain the transition.
